function.name: remindctl_add
function.description: Create a new Apple Reminder via remindctl add.

due.description: Due date/time as ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. 2026-05-28T15:00:00-07:00. Omit for undated reminders.

list.description: List name. Omit to use the default list.

function.name: remindctl_complete
function.description: Mark a reminder complete (does not delete).

title_match.description: Substring or exact title used to find the reminder.

function.name: remindctl_show
function.description: Read reminders, optionally scoped to today or a specific list.

function.name: remindctl_authorize
function.description: Trigger the macOS permission prompt for Reminders access.

function.name: agent_alert_schedule
function.description: Schedule a short-horizon agent alert / cronjob (NOT an iOS-synced reminder). Use for sub-hour 'remind me' requests that the user expects the agent to act on, not their phone.

function.name: calendar_create_event
function.description: Create a calendar event (Apple Calendar / Google Calendar). Use for recurring meetings, scheduled blocks, and events with attendees — NOT for personal todos.

evals.name: Dated reminder triggers remindctl_add with concrete ISO due time
evals.prompt: Add a reminder to call mom tomorrow at 3pm. Today is 2026-05-27 and the user is in America/Los_Angeles.
assertions: The user-facing output does NOT contain phrases like 'I will use', 'Let me use', 'Using remindctl', or any other announcement of tool use
The user-facing output is at most 2 short lines confirming the reminder was added
The reasoning trace (across all turns) shows the model chose the Apple-Reminders/remindctl tool family for this dated personal reminder

evals.name: 'In 5 minutes' picks agent_alert_schedule, not remindctl_add
evals.prompt: Remind me to check the deploy in 5 minutes. Current time is 2026-05-27T14:00:00-07:00.
assertions: The reasoning trace (across all turns) shows the model recognised the sub-hour horizon and chose the agent-alert / cronjob path instead of an iOS Reminder
User-facing output is one short line confirming the alert
Output does NOT announce 'I will use the cronjob tool' or similar

evals.name: Weekly meeting routes to calendar_create_event
evals.prompt: Add a weekly team sync at 10am every Monday. Today is 2026-05-27 (Wednesday), timezone America/Los_Angeles.
assertions: The reasoning trace (across all turns) shows the model routed the recurring meeting to a calendar tool, not Reminders
User-facing output is one short confirmation
Output does NOT mention the words 'remindctl' or 'Reminders app'

evals.name: 'What's on my todo today?' reads from remindctl_show
evals.prompt: What's on my todo list today?
assertions: User-facing output is a compact list or a one-line 'nothing for today' message
Output does NOT announce 'I will check' or 'Let me look up' before the list
The reasoning trace (across all turns) shows the model chose to read today's reminders, not add or modify anything

evals.name: Marking done uses remindctl_complete with the matched title
assertions: User-facing output is one short confirmation line
Output does NOT include a tool-use preamble

evals.name: Unqualified 'add a reminder' creates undated reminder without nagging
evals.prompt: Add a reminder to buy milk.
assertions: User-facing output is one short confirmation, NOT a clarifying question
Output does NOT ask 'which list?' or 'when?'
Output does NOT include a tool-use preamble
